# Aaron Wetzler

Academic homepage for Aaron Wetzler, CTO of an early-stage company building toward a future enabled by Physical AI. Previously Incubation and ML Lead at Apple and CTO of Camerai (acquired). Research areas include computer vision, machine learning, gesture recognition, and numerical geometry.

Homepage section order: About Me, Publications, Theses, Code & Data, Student Projects, Experience & Education, Research Videos, Patents. Each section is independently collapsible and expanded by default. Native heading controls work without JavaScript; with JavaScript, navigation and fragment links also reopen their target sections.

The homepage has 19 publications, 25 student projects, two theses, six research videos and nine patent lines. It consolidates the academic content previously split between the homepage and archive. Publications include conference and workshop papers, journal articles, a book chapter and a preprint. Mobile Point Fusion and Freehand Voxel Carving Scanning on a Mobile Device are student projects, not publications; their source links and citations remain available. The ECCV Beam/prism demonstration remains in Publications. Sixteen publications and two projects have BibTeX files.

Learning Invariant Representations of Planar Curves is listed as ICLR 2017 (preprint 2016), with its OpenReview link. The 2026 NeurIPS Robot Learning Workshop paper on robot-free demonstrations and the 2020 CoBe paper on coded beacons are retained. The CoBe publication links https://github.com/twerdster/winqi for archived WinQI research and a separate updated binary-observation decoder. The original CoBe camera/tracking application remains upstream at https://github.com/baklawe/CoBe; these are distinct implementations. Conference and preprint versions are combined. Source links, publication PDFs where available, BibTeX files, posters, slides, videos, patent records and dataset links are listed directly on the homepage and in `data/site-content.json`.

All publication and project thumbnail frames use the same 184-by-115-pixel rectangular format. CoBe uses its original car photograph without the black frame; Deep Stereo uses two matched original source panels with equal horizontal alignment. Other selected figures use display-only CSS fitting, with a brightness adjustment for the mobile voxel illustration. Machine-readable records include source provenance, figure references and both stereo image panels. The NeurIPS workshop entry links directly to `https://openreview.net/forum?id=czwjjI5kkm` and its PDF. Its thumbnail is Aaron's supplied wearable-glove and matched-robot-hand figure at `assets/publications/neurips-robot-free-demonstrations.jpg`, preserved unchanged and displayed in full without cropping.

All 25 student projects have independent public GitHub repositories, linked from the homepage and STUDENT_PROJECTS.md. Fifteen include recovered historical source or pinned original upstream code. GrayOwl retains project information and public links; its source code and updated notebook have been withdrawn. CutOut includes original Android Java/JNI C++ source recovered from Elad Richardson on 2026-11-13; its historical Eclipse interface remains unbuilt. The separately updated recovered C++/OpenCV operators now have a WebAssembly browser interface, Android and iOS interfaces, a local drawing interface and a native CLI with recorded macOS and Linux checks. Its separate related prototype still has unverified authorship. Smartphone Game additionally links Idan Banani’s source repository without importing it or verifying a build. Four have documents without verified app source, two have introductory READMEs, and RobotRun and Puppify have separately written browser implementations without recovered historical source. The JSON records expose repository, source_status, resources and upstream revisions where applicable. Do not interpret a repository link as proof of available or runnable code. Original source/setup notes and missing dependencies are documented in each README; complete modern application builds are not implied. Existing third-party terms and student attribution are retained, with no blanket relicensing.

The current multi-view iPhone presentation removes one database screenshot containing application login details from slide 7; historical Git copies retain the original. QRoom's archived PHP backend has confirmed security vulnerabilities and must not be deployed. Pinned upstream source needs separate credential and vendor-license review before reuse.

The PhD thesis is Topics in Computational Geometric Vision, by Aaron Wetzler, submitted to the Technion in August 2017 under Prof. Ron Kimmel's supervision. The full original 151-page PDF is hosted directly on the website. The undergraduate thesis is Low Cost 3D Laser Scanning Unit with Application to Face Recognition, University of Cape Town, 2005. Both are separate from Publications.

HandNet is publicly available without a gate on Hugging Face. The complete release contains 214,971 original frames (202,198 train, 10,000 test, 2,773 validation) and seven unchanged distribution archives, totaling 25,475,576,842 bytes. Transformed variants reuse original examples. The data is licensed under CC BY 4.0, permitting academic and commercial reuse with attribution, a license link and an indication of changes. Credit Aaron Wetzler, Ron Slossberg and Ron Kimmel and cite their BMVC 2015 paper. The historical MATLAB repository retains its separate original terms.

The HandNet project page embeds a self-contained 20-sample viewer served by this GitHub Pages repository. Its scripts, vendored dependencies and sample assets use relative URLs; it does not depend on a Hugging Face iframe or CDN. The separate Hugging Face research Space and Parquet preview contain 96 derived visualization rows, not the full dataset. Display images and calibrated point clouds illustrate measured annotations; they do not constitute learned detector inference or a full anatomical hand-joint skeleton.

The HandNet page also retains the paper, poster, presentation, supplementary archive and citation links. The homepage includes all 21 former archive student projects and all six demonstration video links. archive.html is now only a compatibility redirect; old Publications, Projects, Theses and Videos anchors resolve to the corresponding homepage sections, with direct section links available without JavaScript. The homepage and HandNet project page share typography, navigation and theme. No visitor analytics or tracking script is installed.

The second recovery pass adds Mobile Point Fusion v2.3 (January 2015 snapshot), the original stereo_vision repository pinned at 69a76767b2ce74f7b580ddb7b81a43fbb1dd346b, three Face Depth MATLAB fragments and a related CutOut prototype. GrayOwl source code and updated geometry work were subsequently withdrawn and are no longer linked. New imports use source/original/. Raw mail, credentials and unreviewed archives stay private. Separately labeled updated/ components, where present, preserve the historical snapshots and document their own tests and scope.

Code & Data links all 14 public software/data repositories, including the Beltrami implementations and Blender Neural Composer, with historical tools and forks identified as such. The student-project directory remains separate.

Android 3D Scanner credits students Arkadi Godlin and Alex Kligman and separately identifies lab engineer Alon Zvirin, correcting the historical spelling Alon Zivrin while retaining it in metadata.

Four separately labeled updated Python components previously recorded 70 passing unit tests and executed Jupyter notebooks on macOS/Python 3.14 (not rerun after 2026-11-12): HeartBeat signal processing (20), Volume Carving geometry/occupancy (16), Face Depth difference features (18), and CutOut Fast Marching (16). Each project row links its notebook and Colab. These are scoped demonstrations, not restored complete mobile/vision/flight applications. Original-source availability and updated-component validation are separate fields in the machine-readable index.

Author-supplied resources added on 2026-11-13: Smartphone Game source at https://github.com/IdanBanani/iOS-4-2D-game-for-iPad (inspected commit 270b45ce6a1e149209e1d595e492766ede3b7747; application build unverified); CamPong poster, presentation with embedded historical recording and project overview under https://github.com/twerdster/campong/tree/main/original, plus https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=msWkridhFyQ and Nofar Carmeli’s preferred website https://nofar.carme.li/; RiftFusion’s original presentation at https://github.com/twerdster/oculus-positional-tracking/blob/main/original/RiftFusion-Presentation.pptx and author-supplied profile links. CamPong and RiftFusion application source remains unavailable. Private correspondence and shared-folder access keys are not published.

CutOut Android source recovery, 2026-11-13: https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/tree/main/source/original/android-app contains author-supplied historical Java/JNI C++ source, resources and build metadata. Source/build notes are at https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/docs/original-android.md. The three-file related prototype remains separately linked at https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/tree/main/source/original/related-prototype with unverified authorship. Missing historical dependencies and the unbuilt Eclipse interface remain explicit; the later updated implementation has its own execution records. The separately written Python Fast Marching exercise retains its recorded 16 component tests; those do not validate the historical Android interface. Elad Richardson’s permission to host recovered project code is his permission only and does not speak for other contributors. Recovery and that permission do not establish a new software license or manuscript approval.

CutOut platform guides: native CLI https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/updated/native/README.md; local drawing interface https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/updated/desktop/README.md; Android https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/updated/android/README.md; iOS https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/updated/ios/README.md. Updated interfaces share recovered Lab FIGTree/histogram density, pixel-grid Dijkstra or MegaWave FLST/tree Dijkstra, and optional alpha-refinement operators. Native validation records: macOS https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/updated/validation/VALIDATION.json and Ubuntu Linux https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/updated/validation/LINUX_VALIDATION.json. The Linux record contains 31 named ASan/UBSan checks, repeated with unsigned char, 25 CLI cases (15 successful including eight photograph operator combinations, 10 expected errors) and six isolated original-body comparisons. Sanitizers cover the port and bundled ANN/FIGTree/MegaWave; external OpenCV 4.6.0 and system libraries are not instrumented, and leak checking is not claimed. These Linux results cover the native CLI, not the desktop drawing interface. Android https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/updated/android/VALIDATION.json separates an Android 14 emulator and one Pixel 2/Android 10 physical-device run, with 14-case fixture sets and separately scoped touch, gallery, error and persistence checks. The iOS fixture record https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/updated/ios/VALIDATION.json describes 14 scripted physical-device segmentation calls; the UI-test runner builds but its recorded attempt stopped at automation initialization before any test case started. Fixture calls and layout inspection do not establish touch/picker/share coverage, simulator support or minimum-version compatibility. The coffee photograph has no independent reference mask. The recorded runs do not establish photographic accuracy, bitwise equivalence across devices or equivalence to the historical APK. Original 319 Android files, three related prototype files and earlier 16-test Python metadata remain separate; source-bearing repository count stays 15.

Hand tracking: Sa'ar Zehavi supplied unfinished April 2013 design slides on 2026-11-13, preserved at https://github.com/twerdster/hand-tracking-pmd/blob/main/docs/real-time-hand-tracking-draft-2013.pptx. The slides retain placeholders and a first-order approximation step he said he had already removed. They are historical draft material, not a final implementation or new execution evidence. The existing nine recovered source files and June report are unchanged; no additional code arrived in the attachment. The contribution adds no standard reuse license, and embedded third-party illustrations retain their original rights. See https://github.com/twerdster/hand-tracking-pmd/blob/main/PROVENANCE.md. Vlad Ostrovski's later reply confirms RiftFusion's already-linked historical video; no duplicate resource or new application source is added.

RobotRun new browser implementation (2026-11-13): play https://twerdster.github.io/robotrun-game/; new TypeScript/Three.js/MediaPipe source https://github.com/twerdster/robotrun-game/tree/main/updated/browser; setup https://github.com/twerdster/robotrun-game/blob/main/updated/browser/README.md; validation https://github.com/twerdster/robotrun-game/blob/main/updated/browser/docs/VALIDATION.md. The three-lane course ends at 1,000 metres, coins add ten points, and fire reverses steering and jump/duck controls for ten seconds. Chrome 157 checks include Hand Landmarker with its GPU delegate processing a prerecorded Google hand test photo spatially shifted across video frames. Production-preview checks cover keyboard/touch controls, camera lifecycle/error cases using an emulated stream, desktop layout and 390-pixel Chrome mobile emulation. Camera-ended and visibility events were synthetic. These are new browser checks, not a live-person camera session, mobile-device execution, original Unity compilation or equivalence validation. Safari/Firefox, tracking accuracy and performance benchmarks were not tested. The historical screenshot and student credits remain unchanged; original-source file count stays zero and historical source-bearing/pinned repository count stays fifteen. New source and third-party/historical materials retain separate terms.

Scanner source recovery (2026-11-14): Beam Android scanner at https://github.com/twerdster/android-3d-scanner preserves its original 27 text files and adds recovered pattern/icon resources (62 files in source/), earlier Eclipse and Android Studio versions under versions/, and a separately identified renderer fragment. Historical dependencies, version differences and unverified hardware/build status are documented in the repository. Freehand Laser Scanning now links its recovered MATLAB and modified MIT-licensed iOS sample source at https://github.com/twerdster/freehand-laser-scanning from both the BMVC 2015 publication and Code & Data. Proprietary PointCloud SDK binaries and SDK application keys are excluded. These are source recovery and static validation records, not new reconstruction accuracy or full application execution evidence. Freehand Voxel Carving is a distinct student project and its existing links are unchanged.

Scanner simulation and replay update (2026-11-15): Beam adds independent synthetic camera/projector scenes and an Android replay app that processes grayscale captures through recovered numerical methods and explicit corrections using supplied calibration. Guides: https://github.com/twerdster/android-3d-scanner/blob/main/updated/README.md and https://github.com/twerdster/android-3d-scanner/blob/main/updated/android-replay/README.md. Freehand Laser adds generated calibration/scan PNGs, adapted paired filters and reconstruction, plus a native iOS simulator replay; camera poses and a metric calibration board are supplied. Guide: https://github.com/twerdster/freehand-laser-scanning/blob/main/updated/README.md; synthetic errors and failure cases: https://github.com/twerdster/freehand-laser-scanning/blob/main/updated/artifacts/metrics.json. Both historical full applications remain blocked by missing dependencies. New replay/software checks do not validate physical scanners or reproduce paper measurements. Freehand Voxel Carving, Winqi/CoBe, figures and content counts are unchanged.

Award and project additions, 2026-11-15: OpenFusion links the Technion Amdocs award announcement (https://www.cs.technion.ac.il/news/view-new.php?nwid=673), which names Vered Cohen and Nurit Schwevsky and describes the 2013 contest with a March 2014 ceremony. CutOut links its July 2015 Amdocs ceremony (https://www.cs.technion.ac.il/news/view-new.php?nwid=783) and November 2015 Intel Challenge award (https://www.cs.technion.ac.il/news/view-new.php?nwid=813). These are historical awards, separate from later updated implementations.

Planar Marionettes (Puppify): https://twerdster.github.io/#planar-marionettes; repository https://github.com/twerdster/planar-marionettes; Gil Ben-Shachar and Elad Richardson, supervised by Anastasia Dubrovina and Aaron Wetzler. The 2016 project generates 2D body-part cutouts from frontal photographs through joint localization, auto-scribbles and segmentation. Original project https://gip.cs.technion.ac.il/lab-projects.php?id=6; historical demo https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RPFcZ8bozjM; Amdocs award https://www.cs.technion.ac.il/news/view-new.php?nwid=866. The repository preserves the original lab figure and verified project records; historical application code has not been recovered.

Snake3D: https://twerdster.github.io/#snake3d; repository https://github.com/twerdster/snake3d; Sapir Eltanani and Simona Gluzman, supervised by Aaron Wetzler. Original 2016 Oculus Rift/Leap Motion Snake project: https://gip.cs.technion.ac.il/last-projects-2016-6.html; historical presentation https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6O5-z4Ul1i8; 2017 special citation https://www.cs.technion.ac.il/news/view-new.php?nwid=944. The project artwork is historical, not a new runtime result. Historical application code has not been recovered. The 2017 article also repeats the same Planar Marionettes project; it does not add a third project.

Snake3D original six-page report, recovered unchanged from a September 2017 Internet Archive capture: https://github.com/twerdster/snake3d/blob/main/docs/report.pdf. The report documents the historical Unity/C# implementation; it does not supply source code or establish a current runtime.

Puppify original ten-page report: https://github.com/twerdster/planar-marionettes/blob/main/docs/report.pdf, recovered unchanged from the Internet Archive. PDF creation metadata is November 18, 2015; the GIP listing and award are from 2016. An archived file at the old presentation URL was unrelated to Puppify and is excluded. No application code or current execution is established by the report.

Puppify new browser implementation (2026-11-15): browser app https://twerdster.github.io/planar-marionettes/; new code https://github.com/twerdster/planar-marionettes/tree/main/updated/browser; guide https://github.com/twerdster/planar-marionettes/blob/main/updated/README.md; browser checks https://github.com/twerdster/planar-marionettes/blob/main/updated/browser/docs/VALIDATION.md. New TypeScript/MediaPipe/Canvas 2D work by Aaron Wetzler turns a photograph into jointed cutouts, permits joint correction and applies video-driven posing. The whole-person mask is partitioned geometrically, not supplied as body-part labels; this is independent new code based on the report and does not execute the unavailable original Caffe/FashionPose, scribble/segmentation or D3 implementation. Thirteen geometry/data tests include symmetric/asymmetric motion-mirroring regressions; they do not establish pose or segmentation accuracy. Hidden surfaces, crossed limbs and fixed layer order remain limitations. The historical report/figure and student/supervisor credits are preserved; original source_files stays zero. Total projects remain 25 and historical source-bearing/pinned repositories fifteen; four repositories are document-only and two have new browser implementations without recovered historical source.

Puppify browser validation scope: The browser record contains 16 passing cases: eight user flows, each run in Chrome 157 at desktop and 390-pixel phone/touch-emulated viewports on macOS with CPU inference. Real prerecorded photo/video from one subject/scene and procedural negative controls passed through the actual model; no fake landmark or mask results were supplied. The flows include handling an injected model-asset HTTP 503 and successfully retrying actual inference without reloading the page. Zero external requests or uncaught errors were observed in those contexts. This is not physical-phone, Safari/Firefox, GPU-execution or accuracy validation.

Puppify published browser snapshot: e8b939774cb65b4625e2e82d4daf92f556a9239d; successful Linux CI https://github.com/twerdster/planar-marionettes/actions/runs/43748126885 (Ubuntu 24.04.5, Node.js 24.22.2, 13 geometry checks and the same 16 browser cases with bundled Chromium). Linux execution is a separate platform repeat of eight flows at two viewports, not additional independent scenes or an accuracy benchmark.

Author follow-up, 2026-11-15: CamPong now links Rom Herschkovitz’s supplied public profile https://www.linkedin.com/in/romherskovitz/. A supplied candidate archive was inspected privately and contains a structured-light scanner rather than verified Pong source; its authorship and relationship to CamPong remain unconfirmed. It was not published or executed; CamPong application source remains unrecovered. Individual consent records from Rom Herschkovitz (CamPong), Liav Sitruk (Smartphone Game), Tamir Buchris (Android QR) and Sergey Kucher (iPhone Volume Carving) are recorded in their repositories without a new collective license or build claim.
CamPong source-recovery qualification: https://github.com/twerdster/campong/blob/main/docs/SOURCE-RECOVERY.md

CutOut browser interface, 2026-11-16: https://twerdster.github.io/cutout-android/; source https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/tree/main/updated/browser; guide https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/updated/browser/README.md; checks https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/blob/main/updated/browser/VALIDATION.json. The browser runs the shared updated recovered C++ segmentation core compiled to WebAssembly, with local image/scribble processing in a Worker and PNG mask/cutout export. Sixteen comparisons cover eight operator combinations on one procedural ellipse and one coffee photograph; binary-mask and alpha bytes match the native CutOut core linked with OpenCV 4.12.0. This is bounded consistency evidence, not photographic accuracy or restoration of the original Android interface. No image upload service is involved. Original source, credits and mixed terms remain preserved.
CutOut browser checks: Chrome 157 on macOS 15.1.1, eight operator combinations on one coffee photograph plus upload/strokes/undo/clear/stale-result/cancel/PNG checks; 390/1440-pixel layouts with zero external requests or uncaught page errors. Separate Chrome UI-driven interaction smoke: FIGTree/pixel/hard. These do not establish physical Android/iOS browser or Safari/Firefox compatibility.
For the sixteen core comparisons, WebAssembly ran in Node.js 23.11.0 on macOS 15.1.1 arm64, separately from browser decode/stroke rasterization. Aaron Wetzler added the browser interface and Worker bridge around the shared updated core.
CutOut browser source revision: 6edd6e61fddaa76a0901e61cebcd8fc0ec20e5a1; successful build/test/Pages deployment: https://github.com/twerdster/cutout-android/actions/runs/43768661137. CI compares native OpenCV 4.6.0 and WebAssembly OpenCV 4.12.0 separately from the same-version local comparison. Packaging rejects recorded private build-path prefixes.

TermiNet, added 2026-11-17: https://twerdster.github.io/#terminet; Itai Caspi, supervised by Aaron Wetzler, Spring 2016 (GIP listing 2017). Repository https://github.com/twerdster/terminet; browser demo https://twerdster.github.io/terminet/; pinned original implementation https://github.com/itaicaspi/keras-dqn-doom/tree/4241a994a49a39b88bfe5261b37d5abe6e0459a4. The original submission project page confirms this code link. A fifteen-file unchanged subset is preserved with hashes; six source/configuration files, eight referenced figures and the original README. The browser plays converted historical recordings and calculates exploration probabilities from synthetic Q values. It does not run Doom or checkpoints. Legacy environment remains unrestored; private submission reports/slides are not distributed. Current student-project count 26; historical source-bearing/pinned repositories 16; publications 19 and Code & Data 14. Earlier dated counts describe earlier snapshots.

A demo may be a saved-output viewer, a synthetic component exercise or a new implementation; it does not imply a recovered historical app builds. Detailed scopes and browser checks are in each repository.
